## Overview

`estheRineq` unites complex-survey health econometrics and epidemiological health inequality surveillance in R. Every estimator returns a clean S3 object supporting `print()`, `summary()`, `as.data.frame()`, `to_markdown()`, `to_latex()`, `to_html()`, `to_excel()`, `to_word()`, and automated **STROBE-Equity (2025)** methodological notes.

```{r}
library(estheRineq)

svy <- survey_health_data(
  data = survey_mch,
  weights = "sample_weight",
  strata = "stratum_id",
  psu = "cluster_id"
)
svy
```

## 1. Concentration Indices and Curves Across Subpopulations

```{r}
res_ci <- concentration_index(
  svy,
  outcome = "stunting",
  rank = "wealth_score",
  method = "erreygers",
  by = "area",
  favorable = FALSE
)
res_ci
```

```{r}
cres <- concentration_curve(
  svy,
  outcome = "full_immunization",
  rank = "wealth_score",
  by = "area"
)
plot(cres)
```

## 2. Slope and Relative Indices of Inequality (`SII` & `RII`) and WHO 21 Summary Suite

```{r}
sii_rii(
  svy,
  outcome = "full_immunization",
  rank = "wealth_quintile",
  favorable = TRUE,
  scale = 100
)
```

```{r}
w_sub <- subset(who_disaggregated, dimension == "wealth_quintile")
gd <- grouped_health_data(
  w_sub,
  subgroup = "subgroup",
  estimate = "estimate",
  se = "se",
  population = "population",
  ordered = TRUE,
  favorable = TRUE,
  scale = 100
)
who_summary(gd, measures = c("d", "r", "par", "paf", "sii", "rii", "aci", "rci", "bgv", "ti", "mld"))
```

## 3. Reference-Invariant Wagstaff Decomposition and Pelotas Equiplots

```{r}
dec <- decompose_wagstaff(
  svy,
  formula = stunting ~ mother_edu + area + improved_sanitation + child_age_mo,
  rank = "wealth_score",
  method = "erreygers",
  favorable = FALSE,
  bootstrap_reps = 100
)
dec
plot(dec)
```

```{r}
equiplot(
  svy,
  outcome = "full_immunization",
  subgroup = "wealth_quintile",
  by = "region",
  scale = 100,
  diagnose_pattern = TRUE,
  sort_by = "gap"
)
```
